# An exact rational certificate for the remaining symmetric chain kernel

This proves the explicit inequality (S) in
`candidate 9c420d2e51075e2c`.
It is an auxiliary scalar theorem, not a proof of general OC.

## Statement and definitions

Let 1/2<a<alpha=(9+sqrt(33))/24 and 0<=b<=1. Put

    c=1/(3a), rho=1/[3(1-a)],
    A=a/(2a-1), L=(1-a)^2/[(2a-1)(2-3a)], B=(2a-1)/(2-3a),
    k(b)=A(b-c)_+^2-L(b-rho)_+^2,
    g=(2-3a)/[9(1-a)],
    lambda=(18a^3-24a^2+8a-1)/[27a^2(a-1)],
    v=(3a-1)(6a-1)/(27a^2),
    M0=9/2-1/[2a(1-a)], M1=g/(2/9-v),
    M2(b)=3/2+b+(5/2)b^2,
    E(b)=(1-b)^2/6                            if b>=rho,
         (1-rho)^2/2-(1-rho)^3/[3(1-b)]        if b<rho.

Then

    g+(lambda-2/9)max(M0,M1,M2(b))
      +k(b)-lambda[b^2+(1-b)^2/3]-2B E(b) >=0.       (S)

The expressions agree at the piece boundaries. At b=1 only the first
E branch applies. All original denominators are nonzero on the stated
domain, and lambda-2/9>0, since

    lambda-2/9=(2a-1)(6a^2-6a+1)/[27a^2(a-1)]>0.   (1)

We give a finite polynomial certificate covering the full real domain.
The certificate does not infer positivity from point samples.

## A polynomial positivity fact with proof

For a polynomial P(x,y)=sum p_kl x^k y^l of bidegree at most (m,n),
define

    beta_ij=sum_(k<=i,l<=j)
       p_kl binom(i,k)binom(j,l)/[binom(m,k)binom(n,l)].        (2)

Then on [0,1]^2,

    P(x,y)=sum_(i=0)^m sum_(j=0)^n
       beta_ij binom(m,i)x^i(1-x)^(m-i)
               binom(n,j)y^j(1-y)^(n-j).                     (3)

To prove this, for each k use

    sum_(i=k)^m [binom(i,k)/binom(m,k)]
                binom(m,i)x^i(1-x)^(m-i)
      =x^k sum_(i=k)^m binom(m-k,i-k)x^(i-k)(1-x)^(m-i)
      =x^k.

Multiply the analogous identity in y, multiply by p_kl, and sum. Thus
(2)-(3) follow by finite sums and the binomial theorem. The weights in
(3) are nonnegative and sum to one. In particular P>=min beta_ij.

## The explicit certificates

Define F_M(a,b) to be the left side of (S) with its maximum replaced
by M. It is increasing in M by (1). Use the three changes of variable

    b_0(a,y)=c y,
    b_1(a,y)=c+(rho-c)y,
    b_2(a,y)=rho+(1-rho)y,                     0<=y<=1.        (4)

They cover the three branches of k and E. In each branch use its
displayed rational formula, so after substitution all expressions are
rational. In addition to M0,M1,M2, the notation M6 means the constant6.
Set

    J=3a^2+2ay-4a-y+1, D=12a^2-9a+1.

The following are POSITIVE denominators on the parameter ranges where
they are used (the actual domain always has a<alpha<2/3):

    D_(0,M1)=-729 a^4(-3a+y)(a-1)^3 D,
    D_(1,M0)=D_(1,M2)=1458 a^4(a-1)^3 J,
    D_(2,M0)=-1458 a^3(a-1)^3,
    D_(0,M6)=729 a^4(-3a+y)(a-1)^3,
    D_(1,M6)=729 a^4(a-1)^3 J,
    D_(2,M6)=-729 a^2(a-1)^3.                  (5)

Indeed -3a+y<0 and a-1<0. The function J is increasing in y and
J(a,1)=a(3a-2)<0. On [1/2,3/5], D is increasing and D(3/5)=-2/25<0.
These facts prove every asserted sign in (5).

For each row of the table below form the polynomial

    P_(i,M)(a,y)=D_(i,M)(a,y) F_M(a,b_i(a,y)).                 (6)

Cancellation using the rational definitions gives a polynomial; no
remaining denominator is suppressed in (6). Replace
a by a0+(a1-a0)x and y by y0+(y1-y0)y. Apply formula (2) at the
bidegrees displayed. The last column is the exact minimum of the finite
coefficient list in (2):

| branch i | M | [a0,a1] | [y0,y1] | bidegree | min beta_ij |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|0|M1|[1/2,3/5]|[0,1]|(9,3)|3/512|
|1|M0|[1/2,11/20]|[0,1/2]|(9,3)|3/256|
|1|M0|[1/2,11/20]|[1/2,1]|(9,3)|3/256|
|1|M2|[11/20,3/5]|[0,1/2]|(9,3)|13082/1953125|
|1|M0|[11/20,3/5]|[1/2,1]|(9,3)|15032430113/256000000000|
|2|M0|[1/2,3/5]|[0,1]|(6,2)|3/32|
|0|M6|[3/5,2/3]|[0,1]|(8,3)|148954/390625|
|1|M6|[3/5,2/3]|[0,1]|(9,3)|0|
|2|M6|[3/5,2/3]|[0,1]|(5,2)|12664/3125|

Every table entry is a rational expansion of (2),(4)-(6). The companion
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/certify_symmetric_triangle_chain_scalar_root.py` reconstructs the
polynomials and every coefficient with exact rational arithmetic. The
certificate itself consists of the explicit rational definitions and
coefficient identity (2); there is no precision tolerance or sampling
step. Nonnegativity follows from (3) on each entire rectangle.

For a<=3/5, each selected M is one of M0,M1,M2, and therefore no larger
than their maximum. The first six rows prove (S) on that entire range.

For 3/5<=a<alpha, it remains to justify using M6. Direct simplification
gives

    g-6(2/9-v)=(27a^3-44a^2+20a-2)/[9a^2(a-1)].             (7)

Set a=3/5+x/15 for 0<=x<=1. The negative numerator of (7) is

    1/125 + (91/375)x - (23/1125)x^2 - (1/125)x^3.

Its degree-three coefficients in (2), with no y variable, are

    1/125, 4/45, 22/135, 2/9,

all positive. (Equivalently formula (2) gives minimum1/125.) Since the
denominator in (7) is negative before the sign reversal, (7) is positive.
On the actual domain 2/9-v>0, so M1>6. Consequently the last three rows,
together with monotonicity in M, prove (S) for this remaining range.

This covers every a,b in the stated domain, including b=0, b=1 and all
piece boundaries. The closed rectangles were only used for polynomial
certification; no singular original expression at a=1/2 or a=2/3 is
needed. Inequality (S) is proved.
